***The evacuations of [[Shia Islam|Shia]] towns [[Al-Fu'ah]] and [[Kafriya]] in the northern [[Idlib Governorate]] begin, as part of a deal between rebel forces and the [[Syria]]n government. ;Arts and culture
*A joint-team of [[South Korea]]n, [[United Kingdom|British]], and [[Canada|Canadian]] explorers announce the discovery of the wreck of [[Russian cruiser Dmitrii Donskoi|Russian cruiser ''Dmitrii Donskoi'']], off the coast of [[Ulleungdo]] island. ''Dmitrii Donskoi'' was scuttled in 1905 during the [[Russo-Japanese War]]. ;Business and economy
*[[European Union competition law]]
**The [[European Commission]] fines [[Google]] [[€]]4.34 billion for breaching [[EU]] antitrust regulations, claiming that Google abused the dominant position of [[Android (operating system)|Android]] to promote their search product. Google announces it will appeal the ruling. [http://europa.eu/rapid/press-release_IP-18-4581_en.htm (European Commission)] [https://www.npr.org/2018/07/18/630030673/eu-hits-google-with-5-billion-fine-for-pushing-apps-on-android-users (NPR)]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**A migrant boat capsizes off the northern coast of [[Cyprus]], killing at least 19 people, while 25 are reported missing, and the Turkish coast guard rescues 103. [https://www.apnews.com/c6396bd849a74524aa847e6df3943ad2/19-dead,-25-missing-as-migrant-boat-capsizes-north-of-Cyprus (AP)]
;International relations
*[[Eritrea–Ethiopia relations]]
**International [[air travel]] resumes between [[Eritrea]] and [[Ethiopia]] for the first time since 1998. [http://www.france24.com/en/20180718-first-commercial-flight-20-years-leaves-ethiopia-eritrea (France 24)]
;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**Naa'imur Zakariyah Rahman, 20, is convicted of [[Terrorism|terror offences]] after attempting to kill guards, attack [[Theresa May]], and blow himself up on [[Downing Street]] using fake explosives provided to him in a sting operation. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/downing-street-terror-plot-theresa-may-behead-rahman-imran-prevent-isis-a8453391.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Far-right terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
***The leader of the banned [[United Kingdom|British]] [[far-right]] [[designated terrorist group]] [[National Action (UK)|National Action]], Christopher Lythgoe, is jailed for eight years for being a member. [https://news.sky.com/story/neo-nazi-member-of-national-action-jailed-for-eight-years-11440524 (Sky News)]
;Politics and elections 
*[[Cal 3]]
**The [[Supreme Court of California]] blocks [[Tim Draper]]'s proposition to break [[California]] into [[Partition and secession in California|three states]], stating that "significant questions have been raised regarding the proposition's validity". [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/initiative-split-california-three-parts-removed-ballot-state-s-supreme-n892581 (NBC News)]
;Science and technology 
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[Iran]] starts work at a factory that can produce rotors for up to 60 centrifuges a day. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-centrifuge/iran-builds-new-centrifuge-rotor-factory-nuclear-chief-idUSKBN1K80OP (Reuters)]
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Astronomers discover a giant gaseous planet orbiting a pair of brown dwarfs. [http://www.sci-news.com/astronomy/beta-pictoris-b-twin-06215.html (Sci News)]
*[[Environmental issues in the United States]]
**[[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]] Acting Administrator [[Andrew R. Wheeler]] announces coal-burning power plants may dispose of [[fly ash]] in unlined ponds for another 18 months beyond a previously-set April 2019 deadline. Testing standards for hazardous elements in adjacent waters are also weakened. While the move would theoretically save an estimated $28-31 million annually in regulatory costs, there are concerns drinking water could be affected. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/trump-s-epa-rolls-back-obama-era-coal-ash-regulations-n892586 (NBC News)]
;Sports
*[[Formula 2]] driver [[Santino Ferrucci]] is sacked by [[Trident Racing]] for deliberately crashing into [[Arjun Maini]] at a race in [[Silverstone Circuit|Silverstone]] earlier this month and for his sponsor's non-payment. He was previously fined for a number of other incidents, including holding a mobile phone as he drove from a paddock. [http://www.espn.com/f1/story/_/id/24129469/banned-haas-junior-santino-ferrucci-dumped-f2-team (ESPN)]
